pagerduty-bot: ALERT: SLO burn detected — gateway.p99_timeouts > 2s and 5xx spike (count=127) in us-west1 for hosted inference (5m). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pgw/ingress?from=now-15m&to=now :rotating_light:

Ravi (SRE): I'm seeing a sharp increase in 502/504 on /v1/chat/completions starting ~12:02. Synthetic probes show normal latency. Real traffic is the one failing. quick query I ran: `logs.query("service:api-gateway status:5xx | count() by upstream_service")` — most failures map to `auth-proxy` and `billing-evaluator`.

Maya (Support): We already have 3 customer tickets opened complaining "500 internal server error" for regular generation calls (customers A,B,C). They're saying it started ~12:05 and affects small sample of tokens only. Escalation from Support waiting on repro steps.

Ravi (SRE): Dug into the raw logs, sample lines: ```
2026-03-15T12:05:12Z api-gateway id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=auth-proxy err="upstream reset" x-request-id=abc123
2026-03-15T12:05:13Z api-gateway id=def456 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=billing-evaluator err="500 from upstream" x-request-id=def456
```

Aisha (Observability): Tracing shows a gap — many of the 502s have no associated distributed trace past the gateway (trace sampling mismatch). Looks like the gateway is returning early when upstream takes too long or returns unexpected 5xx. Trace IDs: `trace-0a1b`, `trace-0c2d` (I posted them to the trace UI).

Jun (Runtime): Can you paste a raw request that reproduces? I want to see headers — particularly `Authorization` and `X-Customer-ID`. Jun (Runtime) to @billing-service-bot: Can you confirm if billing-evaluator had any errors around 12:00-12:10?

billing-service-bot: billing-evaluator: 12:04:58 -> ERROR rate-check failed for tenant=ten-1234 err="db timeout" 500; 12:05:00 -> WARN fallback cache miss for tenant=ten-5678; 12:05:10 -> INFO healthy. (logs link: https://logs.redwood.internal/app/billing/queries?q=tenant)

Maya (Support): Customer A sent us a curl they used: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
``` They got 502 with body: `{"error":"upstream service error"}`

Ravi (SRE): Quick repro I tried from us-west: 10/20 runs -> 502 within 200ms, others succeed. Error looks nondeterministic. Root cause candidate list: 1) auth-proxy mapping bug that converts some 500s into 502, 2) a billing-evaluator transient DB timeout, 3) gateway circuit/retry misconfig when upstream returns unexpected payload.

Jun (Runtime): I looked at the gateway config — retry policy is aggressive: `retries: 2, per_try_timeout: 250ms, overall_timeout: 3s`. If billing-evaluator has intermittent DB tail latency, gateway could surface 502s quickly. I'm going to temporarily increase per_try_timeout to 500ms for auth-proxy and billing-evaluator routes and disable retries for those upstreams to avoid cascading resets. Applying change in staging -> then to prod canary.

Aisha (Observability): Dashboard panels to watch: `ingress.5xx_rate`, `upstream.latency.p50/p95`, `trace-coverage.missing_spans`. I created a short alert rule to fire if 502 rate > 20/min for 5m and trace-coverage < 70%. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pgw/ingress?view=ops

Maya (Support): Customer messaging: I'll tell affected customers we have an active oncall investigating and that we see transient 502s tied to auth/billing evaluation. ETA unknown; will update in 30m.

Ravi (SRE): Added quick log query to find correlated request IDs to share with runtime: ```
# find requests with 502 and upstream=billing-evaluator
index=prod-gateway status=502 upstream=billing-evaluator | fields x-request-id, http.request.headers.Authorization, tenant | limit 50
```
Found `x-request-id` samples: abc123, def456, ghi789 — cc'ing Jun.

Jun (Runtime): Thanks — investigating kernel logs on auth-proxy pods now. Observed `upstream: EOF` and `connection reset by peer` in the kube-proxy for a subset of pods that were on node n4. Node n4 had a disk IO spike at ~12:03 coinciding with billing DB failover. I'm rolling a targeted restart of 2 auth-proxy pods on n4 and pinning new pods to n5/n6. Rolling restart started at 12:28.

billing-service-bot: Update from billing team: DB failover at 12:03 caused a short window of elevated latency and some 500 responses for tenant-scoped queries. They've applied a patch to increase DB connection pool and are monitoring.

Ravi (SRE): Mitigation checklist we ran: 
- disabled retries to billing-evaluator and auth-proxy for canary traffic (reduces double-mapping to 502)
- increased per_try_timeout to 500ms on affected routes
- restarted affected auth-proxy pods on node n4
- created temporary alert and dashboard panel for customer-impacted tenants

Maya (Support): Notified Customers A/B/C, provided request ids (abc123/def456) and advised they might see intermittent failures for ~15-30min.

Jun (Runtime): After the changes and pod restarts, 502 rate dropped from 5.1/min -> 0.4/min over the last 10m. Trace coverage back to normal for sampled requests. I'll follow up with a runtime ticket to make the retry mapping more explicit (don't convert upstream 500 into gateway 502 without preserving upstream code) — assigning to runtime@redwood with ticket ID RT-2026-314.

Ravi (SRE): Will keep monitoring. If we see recurrence we'll start a full incident and postmortem. For now marking this as "triaged, mitigation in prod".

Aisha (Observability): Saved queries + panel snapshots in ops folder: `ops/ingress/2026-03-15-502-spike`.

Maya (Support): Thanks all — I'll close the escalation once customers confirm. If anyone needs me to ping exec support for a larger customer I can do that. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: NOTE: If SLO burn persists for another 30m -> auto-esc to incident channel.
